findings.claim: The hostile route map binds tuple components to theorem assumptions, finite-model JSON fields, evaluator predicates, positive cases, negative controls, and falsifier boundaries for `T133-MIN`.
findings.failure_mode: `T133-MIN` lists 11 tuple components, but `tuple_component_bindings` binds only non-tuple `minimality` plus `boundaries`. It omits concrete field/evaluator bindings for `carrier`, `realization`, `lawful_possibility`, `liveness`, `residue`, `morphisms`, `operators`, `cycles`, `dimension`, and `k`, and it does not enumerate the executed `FM-MIN-{component}` witness cases. A hostile reader cannot follow the advertised per-component minimality route without reverse-engineering the finite-model payload.
findings.required_repair: Add one binding per listed tuple component, each naming theorem assumptions, exact finite-model fields, evaluator predicate, and corresponding executed `FM-MIN-{component}` case; remove or reclassify `minimality` if it is not a tuple component.

findings.claim: `T133-KLEVEL` maps the declared tuple components `k`, `carrier`, `realization`, `operators`, and `boundaries` through the theorem and finite K-level cases.
findings.failure_mode: The `T133-KLEVEL` route lists `k`, `carrier`, `realization`, `operators`, and `boundaries`, but bindings exist only for `k`, `realization`, and an extra unlisted `lawful_possibility`. There is no binding for `carrier`, `operators`, or `boundaries`, so the tuple-to-finite-case route contradicts the guide/inventory tuple declaration and leaves three claimed components untraceable.
findings.required_repair: Either revise the declared tuple component list to match the actual semantics, or add explicit bindings for `carrier`, `operators`, and `boundaries`; if `lawful_possibility` is load-bearing, add it consistently to the guide and theorem inventory.

findings.claim: The matrix cleanly distinguishes scoped formal model cards from actual phenomenon coverage.
findings.failure_mode: Multiple rows set `counts_as_phenomenon_coverage=false` and say the row is excluded until a domain model/evaluator exists, yet also report `coverage_promotion_blockers=0` with `no coverage-promotion blocker`. That can be read as no remaining coverage gap even though `phenomenon_coverage_row_total` is zero.
findings.required_repair: Normalize blocker semantics: either set a coverage blocker whenever a row is excluded from phenomenon coverage, or rename the field to clarify it only counts attempted-promotion blockers and add an explicit `coverage_gap_reason` for every non-coverage row.
